correctness.rationale: The proof checks positivity and boundedness of each weight, expands the logarithm with an absolutely summable uniform remainder, applies Abel summation to both zero-mean periodic sequences, and derives a quantitative all-k,n product estimate. Orthogonality of shifted basis vectors and dominated convergence handle all three orbit regimes. The failure of strong asymptotic expansivity for negative drift is witnessed by vectors with full bounded forward orbits but arbitrarily late nondecaying mass. Spectral radius, compact perturbation/Fredholm index and boundary approximate eigenvectors give the entire spectral triple. The standalone finite script ran successfully for 28 parameter/start-index combinations; it is only a numerical diagnostic.

value.rationale: The \(j^{-1/2}\) zero-mean oscillation is the borderline where its quadratic contribution accumulates logarithmically, competing exactly with \(\alpha/j\) drift. A single invariant, period mean square, governs a universal critical boundary for every finite zero-mean periodic waveform, including a nontrivial parabolic slice. The complete classification separates strong expansivity, pointwise decay without uniformity, and nondecaying bounded orbits under the same three spectral sets. This is an interpretable, motivated structural threshold rather than a routine single example, an arbitrary finite enumeration, or a small numerical improvement.
